compute.reported_as: For the 36-site simulations, as well as the 108-site simulation at J2 = 0, the plain GCNN introduced in Sec. II A was able to find accurate ground and excited states. We used 4096 Monte Carlo samples and GCNNs with 4 (8) layers of 6 feature maps each for the 36- (108-) site simulations. We trained the 36-site models for 12 hours (approx. 1500 steps) and the 108-site model for 4 days (approx. 2000 steps). All simulations were carried out on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU.
compute.source: Sec. IV (triangular lattice, first paragraph); Sec. II C (single A100), arXiv:2211.07749 (compute pass 2026-09-16)
compute.note: Plain GCNN with 8 layers of 6 feature maps for the 108-site J2 = 0 cluster; parameter count not stated. Steps are "approx. 2000". GPU-hours not stated for this run (only the wall-clock on one A100).

compute.reported_as: Appendix A9 Optimization parameters: We optimized all models using IT-SWO[25]. We used 30 iterations in the inner loop and chose imaginary time constant β based on the relative scale of the energy spectrum for different problems (Table V: Triangular N=108, β = 0.01). Each iteration was performed using adam optimizer[24] with b1 = 0.9; b2 = 0.99 and learning rate that was decayed exponentially with the rate of 0.1 over 8∗10^5 updates starting with 7∗10^−4 ... We optimized all GNN models for 8∗10^5 iterations (≈ 26000 IT-SWO steps). For larger system sizes we initialized the weights with values from smaller system sizes. ... All models were optimized using Google's Cloud TPU v4. All models trained within a day. ... Appendix A8b: All results were computed using MCMC using 2∗10^5 samples from equilibrated Markov chains. ... Appendix A8c: To measure computational efficiency we have timed the process of evaluating 7200 batches of 32 basis configuration within a MCMC process. The GNN-2 model took 17.4 seconds to accomplish this task, while our unstructured ResNet baseline finishes in 2.14 seconds. ... Appendix A6a: Node and edge functions of the Encoder, Processor and Decoder are implemented as MLPs with 3 hidden layers with ReLU activations. The node and edge embeddings have size 64, while hidden layers width 128. We use 6 message passing steps with residual connections in the Processor.
compute.source: Appendix A9 (Optimization parameters, Table V); Appendix A8b (Model performance, Table IV); Appendix A8c (Computational efficiency); Appendix A6a (Model architecture), arXiv:2110.06390 (compute pass 2026-09-16)
compute.note: Row value matches the GNN-2 column of Table IV (separate amplitude/phase networks) for the 108-site triangular cluster. Blanket statements for all models: 8×10^5 Adam updates (≈26000 IT-SWO outer steps) on Google Cloud TPU v4, 'all models trained within a day' (an upper bound, recorded as wall_clock); number of TPU chips/cores not stated; larger systems were warm-started from smaller-system weights. samples = 2×10^5 MCMC samples used for the reported energy evaluation; the training batch/chain count is not stated numerically. No parameter count stated (architecture: embeddings 64, MLP hidden width 128, 3 hidden layers, 6 message-passing steps). Timing 17.4 s per 7200×32 evaluations is a relative-efficiency benchmark with unnamed hardware.
